item.title: New Translations From LTL with Past to LDBA and DPA
item.description: arXiv:2610.15479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present asymptotically optimal translations from linear temporal logic with past to limit-deterministic Buchi automata and onwards to deterministic parity automata. In contrast to previously known translations involving past, the ones presented here are incremental: states and transitions can be constructed as needed on-the-fly, and they do not involve backtracking in order to correct for temporal inconsistencies. The past is naturally encoded in the formula by alternating between weak and strong versions of past operators. To handle the difficulties that arise from the alternation of least and greatest fix-point operators (such as between the "until" operator and its weak counterpart), we rewrite the given formula based on the infinitary behavior of a given word with respect to subformulae rooted with such operators.
item.dc:creator: David Lidell (University of Gothenburg,Chalmers University of Technology), Nir Piterman (University of Gothenburg,Chalmers University of Technology)

item.title: Rabin Games Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.15495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rabin games have their roots in Michael Rabin's seminal work on automata over infinite trees and form a classical model for infinite-round games with Ï‰-regular winning conditions. They play a central role in automata theory and temporal synthesis: translating an LTL specification into an equivalent deterministic Rabin automaton reduces synthesis to solving a Rabin game. In practice, however, Rabin games are typically solved indirectly, via parity games. One possible reason is that many direct algorithms have a factorial dependence on the Rabin index k, the number of Rabin pairs. In this work, we revisit Rabin's 1972 recursive algorithm. The algorithm is implicit in Rabin's proof and intertwined with finite-state determinacy. First, we "excavate" it as an explicit arena-based solver using standard reachability- and BÃ¼chi-game solving as basic building blocks, thus avoiding the exponential dependence on the alphabet in Rabin's original presentation. Second, we show that memoization removes the factorial term from the recursion-tree analysis. Finally, we introduce a variation that recurses on the Rabin index. These results provide a modern analysis of Rabin's recursive method and a basis for studying direct Rabin-game solvers for temporal synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Di Stasio (City St George's, University of London, UK), Moshe Y. Vardi (Rice University, USA)

item.title: Witness Languages for Pumping Lemmata
item.description: arXiv:2610.15500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2022 Dassow and Jecker started investigations on the operational complexity of the pumping constant w.r.t.~two pumping lemmata. Since then, the research on pumping lemmata emerged to several variants for regular as well as context-free languages. Within this work, we further investigate the \emph{witnesses} of regular languages (firstly introduced by Rauch) w.r.t.~different pumping lemmata: For a language $L$ and a minimal pumping constant $K$, a \emph{witness} of a language is a word that cannot be \emph{pumped} by $K$ w.r.t.~the given pumping lemma. Here, the pumping constant is minimal if for all smaller numbers, the pumping lemma condition is not satisfied. Alongside combinatorial investigations on (unary) witness languages, we introduce and study the measure of scattered factor distance, which is related to minimal pumping constants. We present bounds on minimal pumping constants by the scattered factor distance and show that deciding, given two regular languages, whether one of them is equal to the witness language of the second is \coNP-complete.
item.dc:creator: Pamela Fleischmann, Annika Huch, Christian Rauch

item.title: Undecidability of Reachability for Constraint Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.15875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that reachability for constraint automata over finite binary words is undecidable. Eight registers suffice, with conjunctive guards using only equality, proper prefix, proper suffix, and infix incomparability, without word constants or concatenation. Finite-run nonemptiness, Buechi nonemptiness, and bounded Buechi nonemptiness are undecidable as consequences. For Boolean guards over equality, prefix, suffix, and prefix and suffix incomparability, Buechi nonemptiness is PSPACE-complete with arbitrarily many registers and word constants. The upper bound also allows positive infix atoms and yields PSPACE-completeness of prefix--suffix LTL satisfiability.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Michaliszyn

item.title: Track objects in cubical presheaf automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.16376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the formalism of presheaf automata, we introduce new classes of automata for modelling concurrency that extend higher-dimensional automata and symmetric higher-dimensional automata. We study their languages and characterise these languages in terms of posetal cospans.
item.dc:creator: Georg Struth, Krzysztof Ziemia\'nski

item.title: Conditional Membership in Regular Languages
item.description: arXiv:2610.16610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a formulation of regular language membership as a promise problem, which we dub conditional membership: we fix a promise language $P$ and a target language $T \subseteq P$, we are given a word $w$ which is promised to belong to $P$, and we must determine whether $w$ belongs to $T$. We study the deterministic worst-case query complexity of this task, when the length $n$ of $w$ is known in advance and where each query examines the $i$-th position of $w$ for some $1 \leq i \leq n$ and returns the $i$-th letter $w_i$ of $w$. Our goal is to characterize the asymptotic complexity as a function of the word length $n$, depending on the fixed languages $P$ and $T$. Our main result is to show that the complexity of this task admits a trichotomy between three regimes: $O(1)$ queries, $\Theta(\log n)$ queries, and $\Theta(n)$ queries. We further show that the trichotomy criterion is decidable, namely, it is PSPACE-complete to decide which regime applies, given nondeterministic automata $A_P$ and $A_T$ respectively representing $P$ and $T$.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Amarilli, Sebastien Felipe Labbe, Charles Paperman

item.title: Jumbled Simon's Equivalence and Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.17910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: \emph{Jumbled scattered factors} are a generalisation of scattered factors (or subsequences) where a jumbled scattered factor is obtained from another word by deleting and rearranging letters. For limiting the number of rearrangements, we distinguish $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors where $\ell$ limits the number of letters that may occur rearranged. For instance, $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$, $\mathtt{rat}, \mathtt{cat}$ are jumbled scattered factors of $\mathtt{abstract}$ even though $\mathtt{car}$, $\mathtt{start}$ and $\mathtt{cat}$ are no scattered factors and each need one jumble. An example for a jumbled scattered factor with $2$ jumbles is $\mathtt{tatar}$. In this work, we investigate two problems on jumbled scattered factors from an algorithmic perspective. First, we give algorithms for testing jumbled Simon's equivalence where two words are equivalent if they share the same $\ell$-jumbled scattered factors up to length $k$. Second, we investigate how to count the possible occurrences of a jumbled scattered factor -- the jumbled binomial coefficient. After defining the jumbled binomial coefficient, we study jumbled embeddings and factorisations of such as well.
item.dc:creator: Pamela Fleischmann, Annika Huch, Sungmin Kim, Tore Ko{\ss}, Emil Wiards

item.title: Twisted Equations and Palindrome Length
item.description: arXiv:2610.14536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).
item.dc:creator: Volker Diekert, Anna E. Frid, Silas Natterer, Alexander Thumm

item.title: Execution-Time Opacity in (Controllable) Timed Automata is Hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.15478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Timing information leakage occurs whenever an attacker successfully deduces confidential internal information by observing some timed information such as the total duration of a run. Timed automata (TAs) are an extension of finite-state automata with a set of clocks evolving at the same rate and that can be tested or reset. Hence, this formalism is able to represent systems involving timing constraints reacting to the passage of time. Some of the transitions in a timed automaton may be controlled, i.e., enabled or disabled, to limit the runs that are allowed. Execution-time opacity (ET-opacity) aims at studying timing information leakage through the analysis of timed automata. More precisely, the ET-opacity problem consists in deciding whether an attacker can deduce whether some secret locations were visited by a run, solely from the run's duration. When control is allowed, the goal becomes to find a strategy that blocks the runs leaking information. This problem has been shown decidable for TAs, with and without control. However, these existing results only provide upper bounds on the complexity of the ET-opacity problem, sometimes largely above the tight bound. Our main contribution is to provide tight lower bounds for those two results. Moreover, for controllable TAs, two variants of ET-opacity (depending on whether detecting if a run did not visit a secret location represents an information leakage or not, and named full and weak ET-opacity respectively) had been separately studied; we prove here that these two notions are inter-reducible.
item.dc:creator: Sarah D\'epernet (Universit\'e de Lorraine, CNRS, Inria, LORIA, Nancy, France), Engel Lefaucheux (Universit\'e de Lorraine, CNRS, Inria, LORIA, Nancy, France)

item.title: A note on Finiteness and Boundedness in Cartesian Products of Discrete and Well-Ordered Sets, Application to Transition Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.16764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this short note, we prove that any closed interval in a well-ordered and discrete space is finite. The coincidence between finiteness and boundedness can then be established for transition systems where the state space is well-ordered and discrete. Finally, this result is also proven when the state space is a Cartesian product of $d$ discrete and well-ordered sets.
item.dc:creator: Gerard Memmi

item.title: A General Information Extraction Framework Based on Formal Languages
item.description: arXiv:2505.15605v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a terminal alphabet $\Sigma$ and an attribute alphabet $\Gamma$, a $(\Sigma, \Gamma)$-extractor is a function that maps every string over $\Sigma$ to a table with a column per attribute and with sets of positions of $w$ as cell entries. This rather general information extraction framework extends the well-known document spanner framework, which has intensively been investigated in the database theory community over the last decade. Moreover, our framework is based on formal language theory in a particularly clean and simple way. In addition to this conceptual contribution, we investigate closure properties, different representation formalisms and the complexity of natural decision problems for extractors.
item.dc:creator: Markus L. Schmid

item.title: On Epimorphisms of Hypergraphic Automata and Input Symbol Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2606.19394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hypergraphic automata are automata whose state sets and output symbol sets are hypergraphs invariant under the actions of the transition and output functions. Universally attracting objects in the category of such automata are called universal hypergraphic automata; their semigroups of input symbols are algebras of mappings whose properties are tightly linked to the algebraic structure of the automata themselves. In this paper we describe surjective morphisms (epimorphisms) of universal hypergraphic automata and of their semigroups of input symbols, for effective hypergraphs with $p$-definable edges. Under two mild hypotheses, a triple $(f,\mathbb P_s,g)$ is an epimorphism if and only if the state component $f$ is an isomorphism and the output component $g$ is a homomorphism satisfying a lifting condition. We introduce weak and strong epimorphisms of hypergraphs, show that they differ, and prove that liftability yields strong surjectivity under a size condition on edges. For automata whose state hypergraphs are projective or affine planes, the state components of epimorphisms are exactly the collineations.
item.dc:creator: Jasem Hamoud

item.title: Compressed Subsequence Checking is PSPACE-complete
item.description: arXiv:2609.14490v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that the (scattered) subsequence problem for two words represented by straight-line programs is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete, even over a binary alphabet. The lower bound is obtained by a polynomial-time reduction from quantified subset sum. If the two words are given explicitly, i.e., uncompressed, then the subsequence problem is hard for uniform $\mathsf{NC}^1$ and in deterministic logspace.
item.dc:creator: Markus Lohrey

item.title: Quadratic Word Equations with a Linear Side: Polynomial Nielsen Graph Diameter and NP-Completeness
item.description: arXiv:2609.21785v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The satisfiability problem for word equations asks whether variables can be replaced by words so that the two sides become equal. For regular word equations, in which each variable occurs at most once on each side, satisfiability is NP-complete. For general quadratic word equations, in which each variable occurs at most twice in total, satisfiability is NP-hard, but its membership in NP remains open. We consider an intermediate class: quadratic word equations with a linear side, where each variable occurs at most once on one designated side. We show that the Nielsen graph of an equation $U=V$ in this class, with total length $N=|U|+|V|$, has diameter $O(N^{12})$, measured over reachable pairs of vertices. Together with the known NP-hardness for regular word equations, this result establishes NP-completeness of satisfiability for this class. We also show that each strongly connected component is isomorphic to the length-preserving reachability graph of a regular equation, and that the condensation graph has depth at most $|U|+2|V|$.For arbitrary quadratic word equations, we further show that Nielsen paths can be shortened to a length polynomial in the equation size and the number of prefix operations between variables repeated on opposite sides. This yields NP membership for subclasses defined by variable occurrence arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Yonemoto

item.title: Recognizable Picture Languages: Separating UREC from coUREC via Communication Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2609.26047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce communication-complexity lifting techniques into the study of recognizable picture languages. As an application, we resolve a long-standing open problem of Anselmo et al. (2006) by constructing a language in UREC whose complement does not belong to REC. Our lower-bound argument is inspired by the communication-complexity approach to unambiguous automata of G\"o\"os et al. (2022), although its implementation in the setting of picture languages requires substantially different technical ingredients.
item.dc:creator: Antonin Callard, Andrei Romashchenko, V\'eronique Terrier, Pascal Vanier

item.title: The Polynomial Hierarchy does not collapse
item.description: arXiv:2405.18439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The arithmetical hierarchy (AH) is similar to the polynomial hierarchy (PH). Unlike the PH, the AH does not collapse relative to any oracle. A $\Sigma_{k+1}$-complete language is computably enumerable (c.e.) relative to the k-th level of the AH. So, given an oracle in the k-th level of the AH, we require exhaustive search to recognize whether the input string is in the language. We can define a language in AH with a quantified formula and a computable relation. The encoding lengths of the bounded variables are unbounded. However, if we observe only finitely many input strings, then there exist integers such that the encoding lengths of the bounded variables can be limited to these integers without changing the result of the formula for each input string. By adding padding arguments of length equal to those of the bounded variables and padding of length equal to the runtime required to compute the relation, we construct an equivalent language in PH. An OTM operating on the language with padding arguments in PH with a padded oracle has the same program flow as it does on the original language with the unpadded oracle in the AH. The number of oracle queries does not change. We still need brute-force search therefore, the required number of oracle queries is exponential. The PH does not collapse.
item.dc:creator: Reiner Czerwinski

item.title: The Smallest String Attractors of Fibonacci, Period-Doubling, and Thue--Morse Words
item.description: arXiv:2602.16152v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A string attractor of a string $T[1..|T|]$ is a set of positions $\Gamma$ of $T$ such that any nonempty substring $w$ of $T$ has an occurrence that crosses a position in $\Gamma$, i.e., there is a position $i$ such that $w = T[i..i+|w|-1]$ and the intersection $[i,i+|w|-1]\cap \Gamma$ is nonempty. The size of the smallest string attractor of Fibonacci words and period-doubling words of length at least $2$ is known to be $2$. The size of the smallest string attractor of Thue--Morse words of length at least $25$ is known to be $4$. We completely characterize the set of all smallest string attractors of Fibonacci words, period-doubling words, and Thue--Morse words. For Fibonacci words, we show a recursive formula describing the $2^{n-4} + 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil - 2}$ distinct position pairs that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Fibonacci word for $n \geq 7$. For period-doubling words, we show that the $n$th period-doubling word has exactly two smallest string attractors for every $n\geq 2$, and give them explicitly. For Thue--Morse words, we show a formula describing the 32 sets of four positions that are the smallest string attractors of the $n$th Thue--Morse word for $n\geq 6$. Our results show that strings with the same smallest attractor size can have a drastically different number of distinct smallest attractors.
item.dc:creator: Mutsunori Banbara, Hideo Bannai, Peaker Guo, Dominik K\"oppl, Takuya Mieno, Yoshio Okamoto

item.title: A Simple Obligation to Metric Interval Temporal Logic
item.description: arXiv:2607.13598v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Satisfiability of Metric Interval Temporal Logic (MITL) is a widely investigated subject. In this work, we present a new, and arguably simpler, approach for MITL satisfiability, based on an idea of tracking time-constrained obligations along a word. To check whether a Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) formula is true at a position of a word, it is natural to generate certain obligations that need to be satisfied at a later point. For instance, $a ~\mathcal{U}~ b$ (with strict Until semantics) is true at position $i$ if either $b$ or the set $\{a, a ~\mathcal{U}~ b\}$ is true at $i+1$. We enhance this idea in the context of MITL by introducing a notion of time inside these obligations. However, a na\"ive procedure could lead to more and more obligations getting generated along the word, with no bound on the number. We propose a simple mechanism to eliminate or merge redundant obligations. For MITL, this mechanism ensures that only a bounded number of obligations are maintained along the entire timed word. We develop this observation into a symbolic procedure for MITL satisfiability using regions.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Bouyer, B Srivathsan, Vaishnavi Vishwanath
